plain_language: OpenAI bought a startup to keep coding agents alive in the cloud after logoff. A rival shipped an agent that runs a helper swarm on your own computer instead.
findings:
Today's cycle braids three loosely-coupled threads of the same AI build-out, and the dominant one is a clean fork in agent-deployment philosophy that lands as two same-day launches from opposite poles. On the cloud side, OpenAI's June 11 acquisition of Ona (the rebranded Gitpod, folded into the Codex group) buys a product that runs coding agents inside persistent cloud sandboxes, so a multi-hour or multi-day task keeps executing after the developer's workstation powers off and gets reviewed on return; European trade coverage frames it explicitly as OpenAI buying the durable, restart-surviving execution substrate Anthropic dominates inside enterprises, pushing the coding-agent contest down a layer from raw model capability toward who owns the runtime. On the local side, Moonshot's June 12 Kimi Work ships a downloadable desktop agent for Apple silicon and Windows that coordinates an Agent Swarm of about 300 sub-agents directly on the user's machine, drives the logged-in browser through a WebBridge extension, fires overnight jobs through a built-in cron engine with a keep-awake toggle, and leaves original files untouched unless changes are approved - all on the open-weight Kimi K2.6 (Mixture-of-Experts, about 32B active per token, 256K context), the same weights already runnable on-device via Unsloth's 2-bit (UD-Q2_K_XL) dynamic quantization. This split is the day's highest-coherence support: it feeds the durable-ask-user-checkpoint prediction (June 11) at relevance 4 as session-surviving execution with an operator checkpoint on both poles, and it revives the dormant consumer-GPU-coding-agents-displace-cloud-only-APIs row (April 26) as a concrete local-first substitute for a cloud-only API, short of the harness's named resumable suspension primitive and of any developer-share figure.

The open-weights thread is Zyphra's June 12 release of Zamba2-VL under Apache 2.0, a 1.2B/2.7B/7B family of Mamba2-Transformer hybrid vision-language models with checkpoints on Hugging Face: the language backbone pairs Mamba2 state-space layers with a few shared transformer blocks and reuses the Qwen2.5-VL Vision Transformer through a two-layer MLP adapter, cutting time-to-first-token by roughly an order of magnitude on 32K-token prefill, and the small models punch above their weight on perception (the 2.7B posts PixMoCount 82.5, CountBenchQA 87.5, DocVQA 90.9; the 1.2B reaches PixMoCount 62.5, nearly double InternVL3.5-1B at 32.8). It feeds the US-open-weights-frontier prediction (June 4) only weakly as cadence proof with no Artificial Analysis Index figure, brushes the open-weight-text-diffusion prediction (June 11) on the wrong architectural lineage (state-space hybrid, not diffusion, and no GGUF path yet), and revives the dormant 27B-dense/1M-context local-LLM-standard row (April 23) loosely on the local-deployment direction while diverging on every concrete axis. The third thread is corporate-activity: Anthropic's June 1 confidential draft Form S-1 (on a $65B round at a $965B post-money and a run-rate past $47B, more than tripled since February) sets up an IPO season against OpenAI's reported $60B-plus raise at up to a $1 trillion valuation, the backdrop turning concrete on June 11 as SpaceX priced 555.6 million shares at $135 to raise about $75B - the largest IPO in history, eclipsing Saudi Aramco, trading on Nasdaq under SPCX - while OpenAI and Oracle moved to let Oracle Cloud customers route eligible Universal Credits toward OpenAI's frontier models and Codex without a new procurement path. That densifies the supply side of the compute-thesis-IPO-crowding prediction (June 4) at relevance 3 and revives the dormant SEC-compute-prebuy-disclosure row (May 30), but the crowding readout itself is absent: no below-range print, no measured drawdown across already-public AI-infrastructure names, and no SEC action. The summer AI-event calendar runs underneath as forward context only - WWDC26 closing today, the 30,000-person Databricks Data + AI Summit opening June 15-18 at Moscone, and security (Confidential Computing Summit June 23-24, Black Hat USA's AI Summit August 4) plus chip (AMD Advancing AI July 22-23, Hot Chips August 23-25) tracks - so as ever each named landing is gestured toward by today's evidence rather than delivered.
relation_to_my_preds:
The user's first standing prediction (malicious local LLM as malware + zero-trust as fundamental safeguard) is largely quiet on its weaponization and federal-enforcement legs this cycle, touched only obliquely through the trust-boundary framing of the day's two agent launches and with no fresh agent-stack CVE, model-registry compromise, MCP-server quarantine telemetry, or CISA-deadline instrument printed. The nearest signals are control-surface instincts rather than attacks: Moonshot's Kimi Work runs an about-300-sub-agent swarm directly on the user's own machine, files, and logged-in browser session yet leaves original files untouched unless changes are approved - an explicit human-approval gate on agent-authored action - while OpenAI's Ona moves coding-agent execution off the laptop into persistent cloud sandboxes, an isolated container as the substrate the agent runs in. Both treat agent execution as something to contain and gate by default, the same never-trust-the-substrate posture the zero-trust leg names, even though these are product-design choices rather than poisoned-checkpoint or attestation events. On the structural-defense side the only movement is forward-looking calendar: the Confidential Computing Summit (June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint, on confidential agents and secure AI workflows, with AMD, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Samsung and UC Berkeley speakers) and the Zenity AI Agent Security Summit's confirmed New York, London, and APAC expansion stand behind the thesis as venues rather than shipped attestation controls, so the weaponization and procurement-gate legs both sit untouched while the structural answer is staged only as agendas.

The user's second standing prediction (cloud APIs for advanced + local LLMs for daily, driven by SaaS price rises) gains its densest reinforcement in days, with today's agent-layer fork landing almost exactly on the advanced-cloud-versus-daily-local seam the thesis draws. The advanced-cloud leg lands in OpenAI's Ona acquisition: buying a persistent cloud-sandbox substrate so Codex (past 5 million weekly users) can carry long-running, multi-day work to completion is the frontier-workload-stays-on-hyperscaler-cloud dynamic the leg names, reinforced by the OpenAI-Oracle arrangement routing Universal Credits toward OpenAI's frontier models through an incumbent cloud channel and by the IPO build-up (Anthropic's $965B post-money, OpenAI's up-to-$1-trillion target, SpaceX's record $75B raise) underscoring that frontier substrate amortizes only at hyperscaler and public-market scale. The daily-local leg lands just as hard and concretely: Moonshot's Kimi Work runs an always-on local swarm on open-weight Kimi K2.6, and the launch coverage stresses those same weights already run on-device through Unsloth's 2-bit dynamic quantization - exactly the Unsloth-recipe and widening consumer-and-workstation envelope the local leg tracks - while Zyphra's Apache-2.0 Zamba2-VL puts fast, fully-licensed 1-7B vision-language models (order-of-magnitude lower time-to-first-token) within reach of edge hardware rather than API endpoints. No fresh SaaS-API per-token price rise printed to drive the forcing function explicitly, but the day supplies the cleanest cloud-for-advanced, local-for-daily contrast in weeks with hard data on both poles.

The user's third standing prediction (RL/LLM-based forecasting performance improvement) gets a real substrate-leg tick, a thin governance tick, and nothing on real-world deployment. On the substrate leg, Kimi K2.6 is a fresh open Mixture-of-Experts backbone (about 32B active per token, 256K context) whose Kimi Work harness coordinates roughly 300 parallel sub-agents - a concrete read on the long-horizon, many-rollout sub-agent-dispatch surface the leg names - while Ona's persistent cloud sandboxes extend the durable execution an autonomous forecasting agent's multi-day rollouts depend on, and Zyphra's Mamba2 state-space hybrid widens the non-transformer-on-commodity-hardware envelope the leg also tracks. On governance, Kimi Work's file-approval gate and Ona's review-on-return checkpoint are a step toward the per-tenant capability-gating and audit-and-approval perimeter such an agent must run inside before it can be trusted in an enterprise procurement gate, though still without a signed-skill-registry interop result, a NIST non-human-identity control profile, or a formal-verification preprint. The real-world-deployment leg is silent: no physical-AI production-line record, humanoid-policy LoRA, or OEM production-loop closure printed today, with the summer AI-chip calendar - AMD's Advancing AI on July 22-23 and Hot Chips at Stanford August 23-25, plus the AI Infra Summit's physical-AI track September 15-17 - the only forward marker, so the day hardens the substrate leg, ticks governance, and leaves deployment untouched.
